title.narrative: Enhancing In-Site Camp Coordination Camp Management (CCCM) and ABA in Abi-Adi, Axum and Asgede, Tigray Region, Ethiopia”

description.narrative: ltpgtThis enhancing In-Site Camp Coordination Camp Management (CCCM) and ABA project is designed to uphold the rights, dignity, and well-being of displaced populations residing in camps and IDPs living in the host communities by ensuring coordinated, inclusive, and accountable service delivery. The project aims to strengthen community participation, promote safe and dignified living conditions, and support durable solutions such as voluntary return, local integration, or relocation. It will work in close collaboration with local authorities and humanitarian partners to enhance protection mechanisms, foster inclusive site management, and ensure that displaced communities are actively engaged in decision-making processes.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtTo address governance gaps at the site level, the project will reinforce the capacity of IDP committees through structured trainings and bi-weekly coordination meetings. These efforts will empower community representatives to lead site-level planning, dispute resolution, and feedback mechanisms. To support site maintenance and risk reduction, the project will provide essential tools and materials to the committees, enabling them to carry out basic infrastructure upkeep and ensure safer living environments. Additionally, the project will construct communal kitchens and rehabilitate drainage systems to improve hygiene, reduce health risks, and foster communal cohesion.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtA cornerstone of this intervention is the establishment of Area-Based Approach (ABA) coordination and communication centers in each target town. These centers will serve as inclusive platforms where IDPs and host communities can access timely information, referrals, and essential services. By bridging the gap between displaced populations and service providers, the ABA centers will enhance accountability, promote social cohesion, and ensure that no one is left behind.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project is structured around one outcome and three outputs, each directly addressing critical gaps identified in the target woredas:ltbrgtOutcome 1: Displaced populations in both camp and non-camp settings benefit from improved coordination, inclusive community engagement, and safer living environments through area-based CCCM interventions.ltbrgt Output 1.1: Coordination mechanisms and information management systems are established and strengthened to ensure timely, accurate, and inclusive service delivery across targeted displacement sites.ltbrgt Output 1.2: Functional community-based governance structures are established and empowered to lead inclusive decision-making, feedback collection, and site-level dispute resolution.ltbrgt Output 1.3: Targeted sites are improved through risk-reduction infrastructure upgrades, safe access routes, and environmentally responsible decommissioning to support safe, dignified living conditions.lt/pgtltpgtThe project will implement in Axum, Abyi Adi, and Asgede to responds to urgent needs, where displaced populations face fragmented service delivery, weak governance structures, and deteriorating site conditions. OSSHD’s prior experience implementing CCCM projects in the Tigray region provides a strong foundation for this intervention. By building on existing efforts and lessons learned, the project ensures continuity, sustainability, and scalability. The integration of ABA centers further strengthens the project’s relevance by addressing the needs of both IDPs and host communities in a holistic and inclusive manner.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project targets a total of 197,030 individuals, including 176,137 IDPs, 7,141 returnees, and 13,752 host community members. Of these, 53% are women and girls, 52% are children, and 4% are persons with disabilities. A total budget of $249,996.67 has been allocated to implement these life-saving and dignity-enhancing activities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
